name: NY-11
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+10 partisan lean favors Malliotakis
Huge fundraising gap: $2.75M incumbent vs $68K challenger
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The R+10 lean, Malliotakis's incumbency and roughly 40-to-1 fundraising advantage leave DeCillis with no visible path, and markets price her near 95%. With no polls or expert ratings to move the estimate, the forecast stays close to fundamentals at a double-digit Republican margin.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a single-digit race, or a major late outside-spending push against Malliotakis, would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nicole Malliotakis seeks a third term in a Staten Island–based district that leans about ten points Republican. Her challenger, Democrat Michael DeCillis, has raised under $70,000, while the incumbent has built a $2.8 million war chest, giving her an overwhelming resource edge. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which put Malliotakis's chances around 95 percent.

The forecast expects a comfortable Republican win by roughly fourteen points, consistent with the district's lean plus the usual incumbency and money advantages. A Democratic upset would require a dramatic shift in the local environment or a surge of outside spending that has not yet appeared.
